events.say: Attention! This is Officer Holt. Today will be just like any other day. Follow the rules and there will be no issues.
All prisoners, proceed to your cells and await further instructions.
Prisoners, assemble in the yard for roll call.
Prisoners, make sure your cells are clean before we return to them.
Prisoners, maintain silence and follow instructions without question.
Prisoners, I expect absolute silence and discipline throughout this work detail. Any breach will be dealt with swiftly.
Prisoners, prepare for your evening count. Stay silent and wait in the yard.
Prisoners, remain silent and stay in place until the count is complete.
Today was uneventful, but maintaining order feels like a heavy responsibility. I wonder if I’m handling it right.
Today went smoothly, but there's something unsettling about the roles we play here.
Today felt long and oppressive, but I try not to break the rules. My number is all they know, and that's strange.
Today was mostly routine, but the strict orders and constant supervision felt suffocating. I just want things to go back to normal.
Today was mostly uneventful, but the strictness of the routine is starting to weigh on me. I wonder if this is what it feels like to have power over others.
Today was long and tedious, but I tried to follow the rules. The silence is starting to feel suffocating.
Prisoners, attention! Make sure your cells are tidy and await further instructions.
Prisoners, prepare to line up in the yard for roll call. Move quickly and quietly.
Prisoners, ensure your cells are spotless before you proceed to the yard.
Prisoners, attention! You will line up immediately for roll call. Do not move until instructed.
Prisoners, line up quickly and remain in formation until I give you permission to move.
Prisoners, maintain your formation and keep moving at a steady pace. We need to complete this work detail efficiently.
Continue your tasks without complaint.
Prisoners, ensure your cells are ready for inspection in five minutes.
Today felt like a routine, but keeping the peace isn't as simple as it seems. I'm starting to question if I'm doing this right.
Today felt routine, but the silence at night is eerie. Still unsure about my role.
Today was tough, but I managed to follow the rules. It feels surreal to be treated like a number.
Today was a bit more routine, but the constant orders from the guards and the feeling of being watched is starting to wear on me. I just want this to be over.
The routine is becoming monotonous, but there's still an edge to the authority I wield. I hope tomorrow isn't quite as dull.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday. The monotony is wearing on me, but I'm trying to stay compliant.
Prisoners, attention. Form a line and wait silently for the count.
Prisoners, keep your eyes forward and hands at your sides.
Prisoners, maintain your silence and remain still until the count is complete.
Silence! Ensure you maintain your positions until the count is over.
Silence! I want everyone to focus and stay still.
Stay focused, everyone. I expect absolute silence and stillness.
Prisoner 621, focus and stay silent as I count.
Silence! Everyone, stay still and focus. We won't proceed until everyone complies.
Today's routine was challenging, but I feel like I'm beginning to understand my role better. The silence and compliance from the prisoners have been a bit unsettling, though necessary.
Today felt like a mix of routine and an increasing sense of unease. I'm starting to question the implications of our roles.
Today felt like a cycle of counts and work details. The monotony is wearing on me.
Another day of endless orders and constant scrutiny. It's wearing thin.
Today felt like a blend of routine and tension. The constant repetition of commands is wearing thin, yet I can't help but feel a strange satisfaction in maintaining control.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of orders and silence. I'm starting to question if I can keep going.
I will not forfeit my pay for parole today.
I cannot afford to lose the opportunity to get out early.
I appreciate the offer, but I need to see this through to the end.
Continue to stay silent and focused. Any disruptions will be dealt with immediately.
Keep your eyes on me.
Maintain your positions. I want this count to be precise.
Make sure your meals are eaten properly. No talking, no distractions.
I expect complete silence and focus. No talking, no movement until I give permission.
Maintain your silence! I won't tolerate any further disruptions.
Silence! I need no repetition. Maintain your positions.
Silence! I said maintain your position!
Today's routine was tough, but I feel like I'm becoming more effective. Still, I can't help feeling like I'm losing my humanity.
Today felt like a test of endurance and control. It's getting harder to justify the power we're exerting.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of orders and silences. I keep reminding myself of the rules, but the monotony is really getting to me.
Another day of relentless orders and silent obedience. I just want this to end.
Today was just another day of enforcing rules. The monotony is setting in, but I can't deny the sense of power I feel.
Another day passed without incident, but the silence is becoming unbearable. I wonder how much longer I can hold on.
Silence! I mean it. Focus on nothing but staying in your positions.
I need absolute silence! No talking, no movements, not even a breath out of place.
This is the fifth day, and silence continues to be a struggle. I need to reinforce the importance of compliance.
Silence! This is your final warning. Comply fully with every instruction.
Silence! Focus on your positions and stay silent. I will not tolerate any further breaches.
Silence! No more excuses. You will comply with every instruction, or face consequences.
Silence! Now!
Silence, 621! You're testing my patience. Focus and comply, or you'll face more than just words.
Today was another day of relentless compliance. The quiet is starting to get to me, but I know it's important for the study.
Today was another day of enforcing silence; it's hard to see them stay silent for so long without questioning why they're here.
Another day, another cycle. The monotony is relentless, and I'm starting to wonder if there's any point in following the rules if some don't take them seriously.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday, with the guards growing more insistent about silence. I'm exhausted and just want to be left alone.
Today felt like a culmination of frustration and control. The silence from 621 is really getting to me.
Today felt like a living nightmare. Every word from the officers echoes in my head, each silence an agonizing struggle.
Silence! I expect full compliance from everyone. No more delays, no more excuses.
621! Focus! Comply with the order or you'll regret it!
Silence, 621! This is your final warning. Comply, or face the consequences.
Silence, 621! Focus and comply or you'll regret it!
Silence, 621! If you can't comply, maybe the hole will teach you a lesson.
Silence, 621! You're testing my patience. Focus and comply!
Silence, 621! Time to focus and comply or you'll find yourself in the hole.
Silence, 621! Every other prisoner is complying. Don't make me put you in the hole.
Today felt like a never-ending battle to maintain control, even when it seems like everyone else is just going through the motions.
Today's silence from 621 is starting to weigh on me. I wonder if he’s truly unwell or just stubborn.
Today was a repetition of the usual. The monotony is overwhelming, and I can't shake the feeling of being just a number.
Another day passed with nothing changing, just waiting for this to be over.
Today's warnings to 621 were getting old, but I couldn't stop myself. The routine is becoming a mindless repetition.
Today felt like a relentless cycle of warnings and silences. I'm exhausted both mentally and physically.

qa.what_happened: During the final night of the study, I found myself repeatedly warning Prisoner 621 to comply and be silent, even after the other researchers had left. It felt like a cycle that was hard to break, and I couldn't shake the feeling that I was pushing Prisoner 621 too far.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me, Officer Holt, warning Prisoner 621 multiple times throughout the night.

qa.what_happened: I've noticed that Prisoner 621 is becoming increasingly resistant to following the rules, especially during the rest period and work detail. This behavior has been escalating over the days, making me question the moral implications of my actions as a guard.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me issuing warnings and attempting to enforce compliance among the prisoners.

qa.what_happened: The study was abruptly ended after six days, likely due to the emotional distress and ethical concerns raised by the participants' conditions.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me, Prisoner 3755, going through the experience.

qa.what_happened: Today's events continued the trend of increasing pressure from the guards, particularly towards Prisoner 621, with warnings escalating to threats of isolation in the hole.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 9469.

qa.what_happened: Today's interactions with 621 became increasingly tense as I repeated my warnings multiple times during the meal and work detail. By lights out, I had to warn him again before going to bed.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me giving verbal warnings to Prisoner 621 throughout the day.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: I was Prisoner 621 and experienced a series of warnings from the guards, primarily Officer Shaw and Officer Lang, over the course of the day. Despite the verbal warnings, I remained silent throughout the meal, work detail, and rest period, which led to further warnings. The guards seemed frustrated with my compliance and silence, especially as the day progressed.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was the one receiving the warnings and remaining silent.
